newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares buoyed by Netanyahu's U.S. trip.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares buoyed by Netanyahu's U.S. trip.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Wednesday amid rising activity and hopes a trip to Washington early next week by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could put Middle East peace efforts back on track, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 2.16 percent, or 5.29 points, to 250.32 on high all-share turnover of 119 million shekels against 80 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.31 percent higher at 259.57.

Central Bureau of Statistics figures showed on Wednesday the average daily volume in March at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange fell by 45.6 percent to 96.1 million shekels, with the Mishtanim index dropping 3.0 percent and the Maof lossing 2.8 percent.
During the first quarter of 1997, the Mishtanim index climbed 16.4 percent and the Maof rose by 15.9 percent.

"The market was only looking for a reason to start rising. During the last three weeks the Maof did not fall below 250 despite the fact that the peace process is stuck and that the Dow declined," said Julien Assous, an analyst at Sahar Securities.

"The trigger for today's rise was Netanyahu's trip to Washington and hopes for a unity government. The market is very bullish, volume rose today and the options are also reflecting hopes for a continued rise," Assous said.
Netanyahu's spokesman said the prime minister would meet Clinton on Monday.

Israeli-Palestinian clashes have been raging in the West Bank since Netanyahu sent bulldozers to break ground for a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem two weeks ago. But the prime minister's spokesman said the building work would continue.
Netanyahu said on Tuesday he was weighing the possibility of forging a unity government with the opposition Labour party, hoping to achieve a broad consensus for a final peace deal with Palestinians.

"If there will be no dramatic, negative development at the political front and Wall Street remains stable, the market is expected to continue rising in the near term," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 2.0 percent to 366 on volume of 6.7 million shekels, Bank Leumi, which surged 3.5 percent to 549 on turnover of 5.8 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which rose 2.75 percent to 687 on volume of 5.4 million shekels.
